messages:
Vivian: Heads-up — ClearWave (Tier B, committed dedicated pool) reported a sudden throughput drop and p95 spike after last night's push. They say 60% of committed RPS and p95 jumped from ~180ms -> ~900ms. Sales asking for immediate remediation or contract impact.
Sam: Can you paste a request ID or customer trace? Do we have any alerted anomalies in routing/queue depth? :eyes:
Maya: Customer sent a few request IDs in email: cw-req-20260319-11, cw-req-20260319-42. Attaching small excerpt from their span logs.
Maya: ````
TRACE cw-req-20260319-11
service=runtime node=rt-12 queue_ms=42 start_ms=167892 _token_size=320
kv_cache_hit=false batch_size=1
generation_ms=820
````
deploy-bot: Noted deploy: commit 1f4c9b -> 2a7d3e at 2026-03-19T02:14:02Z. Release label: "batching-opt-v2". Canary 5% -> promoted at 02:40.
Sam: That commit was the batching change. If kv_cache_hit=false and batch_size shrank, per-token overhead could blow up. Sounds like a batching regression.
Leo: Oncall suggests short mitigation: route ClearWave traffic to dedicated legacy pool (pre-change) and rollback canary. We can flip routing via runtime-control with this command:
Leo: ```
# route customer to legacy-pool
rictl routing set --customer clearwave --pool legacy-pool --until 2026-03-26T00:00:00Z
```
Jordan: Need impact matrix before we decide product priority. Options: 1) immediate customer routing + rollback (fast, high ops cost), 2) hotfix patch to batching algorithm (engineering), 3) trunk revert (safe but blocks other fixes).
Jordan: Also: this is showing up in roadmap planning: if batching v2 regresses many customers we need to move batching rewrite out of Q2 beta and into Q1 stability work. I need clear numbers from eng to argue scope shift.
Sam: I can do a targeted canary revert for the batching code and run perf tests against ClearWave's traffic pattern. Estimate 2 devs, ~6-8 hours to validate and promote.
Maya: ClearWave is threatening to pause repurchase unless SLA breach is avoided. Sales needs an ETA to convey.
Vivian: We need a committed ETA within 8 hours or they escalate to legal. If revert is fastest, please prioritize.
Sam: I'll start the canary revert now. Will post perf dashboard links when available. If revert shows green I can promote in ~3-4h.
Jordan: Product: marking this as P1 customer-driven. I'll create a backlog card (CW-1229) and tag it for Q1 hotfix lane. Sales, please add customer impact notes.
Vivian: Added impact summary to CW-1229 and pinged the account team. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Maya: I'll keep supporting the customer and confirm routing flip if oncall triggers it.
Sam: Quick note for triage: capture any request where kv_cache_hit=false and batch_size<=2 — those are the most impacted. I'll dump heatmap in an hour.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout action recorded: revert-batching-v2 started by Sam at 2026-03-19T03:05:12Z. Monitoring endpoints enabled.
Leo: If revert doesn't help, next step is to route to fallback model variant (lower throughput but stable). I'll prep the policy.
Vivian: Customer acknowledged temporary mitigation plan and wants notification once traffic is back to baseline. I will update them after Sam's perf run.
Sam: Sharing initial perf: p95 down from 900ms to 210ms on canary. Throughput back to ~95% of commitment. Continuing monitoring.
Maya: Customer confirmed improvements. Keeping thread open until 24h stable.
